root_cause.text: The rockchip GPIO driver fails to explicitly remove generic IRQ chips before removing the IRQ domain, causing the chips to remain on the global gc_list and leak memory because the domain was not created with the IRQ_DOMAIN_FLAG_DESTROY_GC flag.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an explicit call to `irq_domain_remove_generic_chips(bank->domain)` before `irq_domain_remove(bank->domain)` in the `rockchip_gpio_remove()` function. The CVE description states that "the generic chips are not automatically freed when the IRQ domain is removed because the domain flags do not include IRQ_DOMAIN_FLAG_DESTROY_GC," and that "the generic chips remain on the global gc_list and may later be visited by generic IRQ chip suspend, resume, or shutdown callbacks after the GPIO bank has been removed, potentially resulting in a use-after-free and kernel crash." The fix directly addresses this by manually cleaning up the generic chips before domain removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by properly removing generic IRQ chips before removing the IRQ domain in rockchip GPIO driver removal.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `irq_domain_remove_generic_chips(bank->domain)` before the existing `irq_domain_remove(bank->domain)` call within the `if (bank->domain)` conditional block in the `rockchip_gpio_remove()` function.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that generic IRQ chips associated with the IRQ domain are properly cleaned up before the domain itself is removed. Without this cleanup, the generic chips would remain allocated, potentially causing resource leaks or use-after-free issues when the domain is subsequently removed.

candidates.rationale: This statement removes the IRQ domain without first explicitly removing the generic IRQ chips that were registered with it. Since the domain was not created with IRQ_DOMAIN_FLAG_DESTROY_GC flag, the chips remain on the global gc_list after domain removal, causing a memory leak.

The conditional check only verifies domain existence but does not ensure proper cleanup of generic IRQ chips before domain removal. The missing explicit chip removal is the root cause of the resource leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement removes the IRQ domain without first explicitly removing the generic IRQ chips that were registered with it. Since the domain was not created with the IRQ_DOMAIN_FLAG_DESTROY_GC flag, the chips remain on the global gc_list after domain removal, causing a memory leak. The vulnerable code path fails to call irq_remove_generic_chip() before irq_domain_remove().

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit explicitly addresses the vulnerability root cause. In the `rockchip_gpio_remove()` function (lines 801-808), the fix includes: (1) `irq_set_chained_handler_and_data(bank->irq, NULL, NULL)` to disconnect the chained IRQ handler, and (2) `if (bank->domain) irq_domain_remove(bank->domain)` to explicitly remove the IRQ domain before removing the GPIO chip. This prevents generic IRQ chips from remaining on the global gc_list and leaking memory. The commit also adds `rockchip_clk_put()` devm action to handle the debounce clock reference leak. The vulnerable construct (missing irq_domain_remove call) is not present in this version because it has already been fixed by this commit.
